1. (Currently Amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a processing circuit coupled to the ring oscillator and configured to:
apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer to generate a second entropy value;
seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

2. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuit is further configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuit is further configured to:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a single ring oscillator.

5. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators.

6. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer by:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

7. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuit is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer to generate the second entropy value.

8. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuit is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

10. (Original) The system of claim 9, wherein the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

11. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

12. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the one or more logic circuits being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

13. (Currently Amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a single ring oscillator.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer to generate the second entropy value.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the permutation function, hash function, or bit-mixer to generate the second entropy value.

21.
